instruction: Using only the standalone learner-facing English stem, prompts, and opaque token pools, select exactly one condition, two actions, and two parameters. Return the required structured JSON, including exactly one premise row for every opaque token. Do not infer absent client-specific facts.
stem:
A client with type 1 diabetes began a new 45-minute cycling routine after work. On three cycling days, the client developed sweating, tremor, and difficulty concentrating during the ride or within one hour afterward; continuous glucose monitor readings were 58–64 mg/dL. On noncycling days, fasting and premeal glucose readings remain 95–140 mg/dL. The client has no fever, vomiting, ketones, or recent illness and has continued the preexisting meal and insulin plan without an exercise-day adjustment.

Complete the bowtie by selecting the most likely condition, the 2 priority actions, and the 2 parameters to monitor.

actions.label: A1
actions.text: Increase the pre-exercise insulin dose independently.

actions.label: A2
actions.text: Contact the diabetes prescriber or DSMES team to create an individualized exercise-day carbohydrate and medication plan before the next ride.

actions.label: A3
actions.text: Before the next ride, obtain rapid-acting carbohydrate and clear instructions for treating a low reading; follow those instructions promptly if symptoms or a low reading occur.

condition.label: C3
condition.text: Activity-associated hypoglycemia from a plan not aligned with the new exercise routine

parameters.label: P1
parameters.text: Timing and recurrence of hypoglycemia symptoms or readings below the client’s action threshold

parameters.label: P2
parameters.text: Glucose immediately before, during, and for several hours after cycling

parameters.label: P3
parameters.text: Daily urine ketones despite normal glucose and no illness

parameters.label: P4
parameters.text: Resting blood pressure on nonexercise mornings
